office_does: A Grant County Superior Court judge, elected countywide, hears felony criminal cases, civil disputes over $50,000, family, juvenile, probate and dependency matters, and appeals from district court; this seat is for an unexpired two-year term.
race_blurb: Open contest after the appointed judge, Jennifer Richardson, was eliminated in the primary. Ken Chadwick, a senior law-firm partner and former police sergeant who has served as a pro tem commissioner, faces Trevor Bevier, a civil deputy prosecutor with about 12 years of private practice. No bar rating was found for either.

candidates.summary: Senior partner at STW Law PLLC in Ephrata with 23 years of practice, mostly civil, after 15 years as a police officer and sergeant; has served as an arbitrator, mediator and pro tem superior court commissioner.
highlights: Attorney since 2003; partner at STW Law PLLC since 2009 [S1][S3]
Pro tem commissioner, arbitrator and mediator in Grant County Superior Court (self-reported) [S1][S3]
Police officer and sergeant for 15 years before law school [S1][S3]
Proposes local court-rule changes and more courtroom space to cut litigation costs [S3]
Endorsed by retired Chief Justice Barbara Madsen, retired Judge John Knodell and District Court Judge Nicholas Wallace [S2]

experience.basis: Not an incumbent, but runs on 23 years of practice and quasi-judicial service as arbitrator, mediator and pro tem commissioner.

safety.basis: Professional formation includes 15 years as a police officer and sergeant in patrol and detective units; his law practice is mostly civil and he has stated no bail or diversion position.

candidates.summary: Grant County civil deputy prosecuting attorney since 2025 after about 14 years as a legal intern and associate at a Moses Lake firm; earlier worked in title insurance and real estate. Has no judicial or pro tem service.
highlights: Civil deputy prosecuting attorney for Grant County since 2025 [S1][S3]
Private civil practice in Moses Lake: litigation, real estate, probate, bankruptcy, family law [S1][S2]
Pledges timely decisions that explain their reasoning [S2][S3]
Endorsed by Prosecuting Attorney Brandon Guernsey and retired Judge Richard Fitterer [S1][S3]

experience.basis: Established legal career (about 12 years of practice, now a deputy prosecutor) but no judicial or quasi-judicial service; pitches community roots and real-world experience rather than tenure.
